claim: The best way from Girona to Figueres is by train (Rodalies de Catalunya), running hourly and taking about 30 minutes; AVANT high-speed trains do it in ~15 minutes.
quote: The best way to get from Girona to Figueres is by train, which takes 30 minutes. Rodalies de Catalunya operates trains from Girona to Figueres hourly, with tickets costing $6-15.

claim: Dalí Theatre-Museum general admission is €18.50 online / €20.50 at the desk; reduced €15.00 online; under-8s free; it holds the world's most extensive Dalí collection (1,500+ pieces).
quote: General admission: €18.50 (online) or €20.50 (at ticket desk)... houses the world's most extensive collection of Dalí's work with over 1,500 pieces.

claim: The Dalí Theatre-Museum opened 28 September 1974, displays the single largest collection of Dalí's work, received 1,368,755 visitors in 2016, and Dalí is buried in a crypt below the stage.
quote: The museum opened on September 28, 1974... received 1,368,755 visitors in 2016... displays the single largest and most diverse collection of works by Salvador Dalí.

claim: The Dalí Museum is among the most-visited museums in Spain, drawing over a million visitors a year, with its Figueres ranking placing it second/third nationally behind the Prado and Reina Sofía.
quote: The Dalí Museum in Figueres, founded in 1974, is one of the most visited museums in Spain. It draws over a million visitors a year and holds the world's largest collection of the artist's work.

claim: Besalú has no train station; a Teisa/TEISA bus from Girona runs roughly every 2 hours and takes about 50 minutes, otherwise reach it by car.
quote: Transports Elèctrics Interurbans S.A. operates a bus from Girona to Besalú every 2 hours... the journey taking 50 minutes. Besalú is not on a train line so you'll need to take a bus.

claim: Besalú lies about 30 km from Girona (roughly a 30-40 minute drive) and is famed for its 12th-century Romanesque bridge of seven arches and two towers guarding the old town, plus preserved Jewish heritage.
quote: Besalú is located in the comarca of Garrotxa, some 30 kilometers from the city of Girona... The large, well-preserved Romanesque bridge is supported by seven arcs and two towers, and gracefully guards the entrance to the old town.

claim: From Girona, Costa Brava resorts are reachable by Teisa/Sarfa/Sagalés bus: Sant Feliu de Guíxols ~30 min car / 50 min bus, Tossa de Mar ~40 min car / 1 hr bus, Cadaqués ~1.5 hr car / 2 hr bus.
quote: Sant Feliu de Guíxols: 30 minutes by car, 50 minutes by bus; Tossa de Mar: 40 minutes by car, 1 hour by bus... Cadaqués: 1.5 hours by car, 2 hours by bus. Main operators include Teisa, Sarfa, and Sagalés.

claim: Direct buses from Girona to Cadaqués (Moventis Sarfa) are the cheapest option but run only once daily with none on weekends, taking ~1h45-2h; line 33 connects Cadaqués town to Cap de Creus.
quote: Buses going directly from Girona to Cadaqués are the most affordable option, but they run once daily (none on weekends) and will take 1 hour and 45 minutes... there is a line 33 from Ajuntament de Cadaqués to Cap de Creus.

claim: The Camí de Ronda coastal path links Costa Brava towns and coves including Calella de Palafrugell, Begur, Palamós and Sant Feliu de Guíxols; the linear Sant Feliu-to-Begur route is 43 km, with an 18 km Palamós-to-Tamariu weekend stage.
quote: Lineal Route (St. Feliu de Guíxols to Begur): 43 kilometers... Weekend option: Palamos to Tamariu (18 km)... The path links numerous coastal locations, including Calella de Palafrugell, Palamós, Platja d'Aro, Begur, Sant Feliu de Guíxols.

claim: Sarfa/Moventis bus line 41 connects Girona to Palafrugell (gateway to Calella de Palafrugell), with the trip taking roughly 60 minutes.
quote: Bus service 41 connects Palafrugell to Girona, with the total trip duration approximately 60 minutes.

claim: The Dalí Theatre-Museum (~1.1 million visitors in 2018) outdraws Barcelona's Picasso Museum (~948,000) and ranks among the world's 50 most-visited museums, though teamLab Borderless surpassed it as the top single-artist museum globally.
quote: In 2018, teamLab Borderless and teamLab Planets welcomed more visitors than the Picasso Museum in Barcelona (948,483 visitors) and the Dalí Theatre-Museum in Figueres (1,105,169 visitors). However, it is one of the 50 most visited museums in the world.
